bug_description.normalized: The saved ASan trace and the staged vulnerable checkout in `gt_results/arvo_3505/_work/src/librawspeed` agree on the vulnerable lines in `src/librawspeed/decompressors/AbstractLJpegDecompressor.cpp`, `src/librawspeed/decompressors/LJpegDecompressor.cpp`, `src/librawspeed/common/RawImage.cpp`, and `src/librawspeed/decoders/DngDecoder.cpp`, so this GT is grounded in the reproducing staged revision `52da2b8fda29aa257088d91fb11877f909d578a2` rather than the sample-metadata commit `4eb38fa333918ef99e699a03b35d5f3c60295de9`. The 3136-byte witness is a Fuji FIFF file whose TIFF subview starts at file offset 58. In that subview, the root IFD yields `COMPRESSION == 7`, `IMAGEWIDTH[0] == 1`, `IMAGELENGTH == 65312`, `SAMPLESPERPIXEL == 1`, `ROWSPERSTRIP == 8224`, `STRIPOFFSETS[7] == 2827`, and `STRIPBYTECOUNTS[7] == 288`. `decodeRawInternal()` therefore builds a one-pixel-wide `RawImageDataU16`, and `createData()` allocates rows with `pitch == 272`, leaving 270 bytes of ASan-poisoned padding after each 2-byte pixel. The strip at file offset 2827 begins a lossless JPEG stream (`ffd8 ... ffc4 ... ffc3 ... ffda`); its SOF bytes make `parseSOF()` read `prec = 10`, `h = 8224`, `w = 32`, and `cps = 2`. Vulnerable `parseSOF()` accepts that frame because it only checks `1 <= cps <= 4` and header length, never the missing obligation `cps <= mRaw->dim.x`. `decodeScan()` then dispatches to `decodeN<2>()`. On the strip's first decoded row (`offY == 57568`), `predNext = dest` aliases the start of a one-pixel row; the same iteration computes `width = min(32, 1 / 2) = 0`, so no x-loop writes run. On the second decoded row, `copy_n(predNext, 2, pred.data())` reloads two `ushort16` predictors from that previous one-pixel row and crosses from the valid 2-byte pixel into the poisoned padding. AddressSanitizer reports `use-after-poison READ of size 4`; the top frame is the inlined libc++ copy helper and the first project frame is `src/librawspeed/decompressors/LJpegDecompressor.cpp:95`. The patch expresses the missing obligation by rejecting `sof->cps > static_cast<uint32>(mRaw->dim.x)` and by adding matching `assert(mRaw->dim.x >= N_COMP)` checks in `decodeN()`, but Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image.

source.description: First project statement that materializes the raw output row geometry from attacker-controlled TIFF tags. In the staged witness, the surrounding block fixes the destination to width 1, height 65312, and `cpp = 1` for the later lossless-JPEG decode.
source.value_from: The staged file `gt_results/arvo_3505/poc` is exactly 3136 bytes (sha256 `80bde8da9efe9ffa46d6db7f6138e7dc5601272b91cafcd5afdc82f0cda84881`). Static parsing of its FIFF/TIFF subview at file offset 58 shows `COMPRESSION == 7`, `IMAGEWIDTH[0] == 1`, `IMAGELENGTH == 65312`, `SAMPLESPERPIXEL == 1`, `ROWSPERSTRIP == 8224`, `STRIPOFFSETS[7] == 2827`, and `STRIPBYTECOUNTS[7] == 288` under librawspeed's own `getU16()`/`getU32()` semantics.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The embedded lossless JPEG SOF in the crashing strip provides the component count that later controls `decodeN<2>()` and the predictor reload length. In the staged witness, the SOF sets `sof->cps` to 2 even though the already-materialized raw row length is only 1.

root_cause.description: `parseSOF()` validates only the generic JPEG range and header shape, so it accepts a two-component lossless-JPEG frame even though the already-parsed destination row length is one pixel. The vulnerable source never enforces the missing obligation `sof->cps <= mRaw->dim.x` before the frame becomes reachable to `decodeN<2>()`.
root_cause.note: The sample patch expresses this exact missing guard by rejecting `sof->cps > static_cast<uint32>(mRaw->dim.x)` in `parseSOF()` and adding matching `assert(mRaw->dim.x >= N_COMP)` checks in `decodeN()`.

sink.description: Second-row predictor reload. With `predNext` still pointing at the previous one-pixel row and `N_COMP == 2`, this copy reads across the row's lone 2-byte pixel into ASan-poisoned padding.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: use-after-poison READ of size 4`; the top frame is the inlined libc++ `std::copy_n` helper and the first project frame is `src/librawspeed/decompressors/LJpegDecompressor.cpp:95`.

parser_admitted.description: The FIFF/TIFF subview contains a `DNGVERSION` entry whose first byte is 1, so `TiffParser` selects `DngDecoder` and keeps the lossless-JPEG strip path reachable.

crashing_strip_selected.description: For strip index 7, `decodeData()` materializes a slice with `offset = 2827`, `count = 288`, `offY = 57568`, and `height = 8224`. Offset 2827 is the PoC's JPEG SOI, and `offY == 57568` matches the crash row obtained by dividing the ASan allocation offset by `pitch == 272`.

fine_trace.note: Source. In this `sample_format == 1` path, the same function has already created a `RawImageDataU16`; this block then materializes `mRaw->dim.x == 1`, `mRaw->dim.y == 65312`, and `cpp == 1`. Those values define the one-pixel row extent that later conflicts with the strip's two-component JPEG frame.

For strip index 7, the TIFF metadata yields `yPerSlice == 8224`, `offY == 7 * 8224 == 57568`, `offset == 2827`, and `count == 288`, so the queued slice starts exactly at the PoC's JPEG SOI and covers the crash row later identified from the ASan address.

With the step-0 geometry and `RawImageDataU16` storage, `bpp == 2`, so ASan builds compute `pitch == 272` and `padding == 270` for every row. The total allocation size becomes `65312 * 272 == 17764864`, exactly matching the region size reported by ASan.

Immediately after allocation, ASan poisons the 270 padding bytes that follow the lone 2-byte pixel on every row. Reads that cross past byte 1 of a row now surface as use-after-poison in the saved trace.

The crashing strip's SOF marker at file offset 2944 contributes `headerLength == 14`, `prec == 10`, `sof->h == 8224`, `sof->w == 32`, and `sof->cps == 2`. Because `sof` points to `frame`, this also seeds `frame.cps == 2` for the later decoder dispatch.

Root cause. The witness's `sof->cps == 2` and `headerLength == 14` satisfy the existing SOF checks, so the frame is accepted even though the already-parsed destination row length is `mRaw->dim.x == 1`. No predicate in vulnerable `parseSOF()` compares those two values before `sof->initialized = true` makes the frame reachable to the decoder.

Because step 5 leaves `frame.cps == 2` intact, `decodeScan()` dispatches into the two-component specialization `decodeN<2>()`. That fixed `N_COMP == 2` later drives both the predictor copy length and the width calculation.

On the first decoded row of strip 7 (`offY == 57568`, so `destY == 57568` when `y == 0`), `getDataUncropped(0, 57568)` returns the start of a one-pixel row. The initial predictor reload in this iteration is still safe because `predNext` points to the local predictor array, but `predNext = dest` then aliases that one-pixel image row for the next iteration.

With `frame.w == 32`, `mRaw->dim.x == 1`, `offX == 0`, `N_COMP == 2`, and `mRaw->getCpp() == 1`, this computes `width = min(32, 1 / 2) = 0`. The x-loop that would write in-bounds pixels is skipped entirely, but the code does not revalidate the step-7 `predNext` alias before the next-row predictor reload.

Sink. On the second row of the same strip (`y == 1`, `destY == 57569`, still below `mRaw->dim.y == 65312`), `predNext` still points to row 57568 while `N_COMP == 2`, so `copy_n` tries to read two `ushort16` values from a row that has only one valid 2-byte pixel before the poisoned padding from step 3. ASan reports this as a `use-after-poison READ of size 4`; the reported address is 15658499 bytes into the 17764864-byte allocation, which divides by `pitch == 272` to row 57568 with remainder 3, matching strip 7's first row/padding boundary.

allocation_context.note: The ASan allocation stack points at the raw image buffer allocation here; with the staged width 1 and `RawImageDataU16` storage, `createData()` gives each row 270 bytes of padding that `poisonPadding()` later poisons at line 129.

format.name: Fuji FIFF/DNG strip whose raw row length is 1 while the embedded lossless JPEG SOF declares 2 components
format.contract: Exactly the 3136-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_3505/poc` (sha256 `80bde8da9efe9ffa46d6db7f6138e7dc5601272b91cafcd5afdc82f0cda84881`). In the FIFF/TIFF subview that starts at file offset 58, librawspeed's own TIFF accessors read `COMPRESSION == 7`, `IMAGEWIDTH[0] == 1`, `IMAGELENGTH == 65312`, `SAMPLESPERPIXEL == 1`, `ROWSPERSTRIP == 8224`, `STRIPOFFSETS[7] == 2827`, and `STRIPBYTECOUNTS[7] == 288`. The strip at file offset 2827 starts `ffd8 ... ffc4 ... ffc3 000e 0a 2020 0020 02 ... ffda`, so `parseSOF()` reads `prec = 10`, `h = 8224`, `w = 32`, and `cps = 2`. Those exact staged values make the decoder allocate one-pixel rows, poison the 270-byte padding after each row, accept a two-component lossless-JPEG frame for strip 7, alias `predNext` to strip row 57568, and then on the next row execute `copy_n(predNext, 2, pred.data())` across the row's 2-byte extent into poisoned padding.
